parts.text: Fig. 3.1 shows gas trapped in the sealed end of a tube by a dense liquid. Fig. 3.1 The scale marked on the sealed end of the tube is calibrated to read the volume of gas trapped above the liquid surface. Fig. 3.1 shows that initially the volume V 1 of the gas is 60 cm 3 . The pressure of the atmosphere is 1.0 × 10 5 Pa.

ms.text: liquid levels in the two limbs of the tube are equal

ms.text:
molecules collide with the walls (of the container)
momentum of molecules changes (reverses)
this causes a force AND force spread out (over area of walls)

parts.text: (c) More of the dense liquid is poured into the open end of the tube. The level of the liquid surface in both the sealed and the open ends of the tube rises as shown in Fig. 3.2. The temperature of the trapped gas and atmospheric pressure both remain constant. Fig. 3.2
